title: GraphSmith Coding-Session Trace
description: A raw Claude Code or Codex coding-agent session log, normalized into an ordered stream of file-touch events. Adapter-produced, deterministic. A read-only observational record -- makes no claim about whether the session's work was correct, safe, or complete, and no claim about test outcomes beyond 'a command shaped like a verify command ran, and whether the tool call itself errored.' Distinct from GraphSmith's own GSA execution_trace (Lane E's domain) -- this describes an upstream coding CLI's own session, not a GraphSmith-orchestrated run.

id.description: Harness-reported session id, display-only. NOT a safe routing or cache key -- Codex resume rollouts can reuse an id across multiple session files.

sourcePath.description: Absolute path to the session JSONL file this trace was parsed from.

sourceLines.description: Total JSONL lines read, including unparseable/skipped ones.

unresolved.description: true when this call never received a matching result before the session log ended -- its isError:false is NOT a confirmed non-error, just the absence of any result. Omitted (not written as false) for a normally-resolved event. When any event in a trace has this set, stats.observability.errors is downgraded to 'estimated' even for a harness that otherwise reports a structural error flag.

summary.description: One-line, mechanically generated description of the call -- never free prose.

filesInRepo.description: Set only when the repo is available to count against at parse time; observability.repoSize flags whether this is trustworthy.

touched.description: Distinct files appearing as any target across all events. [Fixed per adversarial review -- MEDIUM: mindwalk's own schema has no equivalent of this field -- mindwalk tracks 'edited' only. Disclosed here explicitly as a genuinely new field, not silently added as if it were a port; kept because 'files touched vs. files actually edited' is useful signal for a report and cheap to compute from data the trace already has.

churnFiles.description: Files edited in three or more events.

editsAfterLastVerify.description: Edit events after the last verify-classified event. NOTE: 'verify' means a command shaped like a test/build runner ran -- not that it passed.

verifyOutcome.description: Always 'unavailable' in v1: 'verify' actions are a command-shape classification only. Explicitly out of scope for the first build.

weak.description: true when the path was inferred from free-text rather than a structured tool argument.
